newsitem.title: QATAR: India seeks stake in Qatar LNG project.
newsitem.headline: India seeks stake in Qatar LNG project.

text.p: India is looking for a stake in Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG Co (Rasgas) and has offered to buy up to five million tonnes a year of gas for 25 years from 2001, a senior Indian official said.
"The two things are not interlinked, but we would prefer a deal that way if the Qatari authorities agreed," said R.P. Sharma, director of Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL).
Sharma said the current talks with Qatar are focused on "4-5 million tonnes of LNG to meet short-term needs."
"But for larger volumes, we need to have a concessionary right to explore and develop a gas field, or partnership in a major gas project, like Mobil or Enron have in Qatari LNG projects," he said.

Sharma, part of an Indian government delegation to Qatar to discuss a gas supply deal, told Reuters: "We have submitted a proposal to the Qatari authorities and they have up to January 15 to respond."
"We have told them that they can also take up to a 50 percent stake in a consortium we are setting up, to build a string of regassification facilities and LNG terminals in India," he said.
The state's Qatar General Petroleum Corp has 66.5 percent in Rasgas, Mobil Corp has 26.5 percent, Japan's Nissho Iwai has four and Itochu Corp three percent.

Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, declined to comment on the Indian request for equity participation in Rasgas but he said the offer to invest in a consortium could be considered.
"Qatar is willing to cooperate in all investments in India realising its ability to absorb large gas volumes which Qatar can supply," he told Reuters.

Sharma said the proposed consortium would be 50 percent owned by three Indian public sector companies -- GAIL, Oil and Natural Gas Commission (ONGC) and Indian Oil Corp (IOC) - and the rest is on offer to a company which supplies the gas.

Sharma said the consortium is planning to build LNG terminals and regassification facilities to handle 2.5 million tonnes a year each at Ennore in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu and New Mangalore, also in south India.

"But considering our rising energy needs we will have to build many more terminals in other parts of the country. We estimate that our energy consumption would go up to 200 billion cubic metres a day of gas equivalent - or 50 million tonnes a year of LNG - by the year 2010," he said.
